title: Addon doc-set structure (documentation-§1/§2/§3) and release notes
cluster_summary: All eight findings are real, local doc-shape or release-note drift. Each fix belongs in the addon's own README.md, CLAUDE.md or docs/, and no single upstream change would make any of them moot. Two of them are recurrences that an upstream check would prevent: SD-FIN-01's sync-docs pass deleted PFE's empty Tier 3 table, and PM has reintroduced angle-bracket placeholders. Those checks are optional dev-copilot follow-ups, not blockers. Recommendation: one small docs commit per addon (LH: README close, 1.4.0 row and map list; PM: placeholders, 1.2.0 row and stub order; PFE: Tier 3 heading; MM: release-note sentence), each followed by a de-AI pass. Delete the contributor-facing 'Released on lint, tests and complexity only' lines in LH and PM rather than prefixing them. Correct MM's sentence to the old path actually shipped, minimap.hide, and to its real value semantics. The PFE settings-panel reshape is optional.

verdicts.assessment: README.md:63 closes on two sentences, but documentation-§1 item 5 asks for one signpost sentence and no deviation row covers it. The cost is close to zero because the README is already being edited for LH-A-07.
verdicts.remediation: Fold into the LH-A-07 README commit. Merge the close into one sentence naming Settings → AddOns and /lh help, plus the long form where item 5 asks for it, then run the de-AI pass.

verdicts.assessment:
The unprefixed '
Released on lint, tests and complexity only…' line in the 1.4.0 row is contributor test-gate material in the player-facing table that ships to CurseForge. The defect is item 11's player-facing rule and '- ' prefix rule. The line is not 'now false': it still accurately records how 1.4.0 was gated.
verdicts.remediation: Delete the line from the 1.4.0 row. Do not just add a '- ' prefix. Then run the de-AI pass.

verdicts.assessment: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:327's out-of-scope list omits docs/perf-analysis/<run>/. That leaves docs/perf-analysis/20261007-104651/ in no table and will recur with every capture. The list also freezes all of docs/automated-tests/, even though two of its files are registered.
verdicts.remediation: Replace the list with documentation-§3's own: docs/audits/, docs/reviews/, docs/automated-tests/<run>/, docs/perf-analysis/<run>/, docs/revendor/<date>-v<tag>/, docs/superpowers/ (and docs/investigations/ when present).

verdicts.assessment: PFE is the only addon whose Documentation map lacks the fourth table, '### Addon-specific (documentation-§3, Tier 3)', which bc3c941 (SD-FIN-01) deleted. The standard fixes four tables. Every doc is still registered, but a one-line restore stops the finding recurring in every audit.
verdicts.remediation: Restore '### Addon-specific (documentation-§3, Tier 3)' after Verification and record, with a '| Doc | Covers |' header and 'None.'. Optional upstream follow-up: have dev-copilot sync-docs keep the four-table skeleton when a table empties.

verdicts.assessment: documentation.md:258 states the settings-panel.md shape firmly: a Page | Covers table with one row per subcategory page, and a page → tab → row tree with one heading per page. That makes this low, not info. But the existing Page|Tab|Covers doc is a correct superset that agrees with the schema, and a reshape has no reader benefit. It is cheap mechanical churn, best done alongside the PFE-A-04 edit or the next settings change.
verdicts.remediation: Reshape docs/settings-panel.md to a Page | Covers table with one row per subcategory page, then one '## <Page>' heading per page with '### <Tab>' sub-headings in group declaration order. Content stays unchanged.

verdicts.assessment: documentation-§2 requires the stub items 'in this order', and the provenance line (item 6, :45) sits before the green-gate line (item 5, :62). This is a pure move with no content change, and it can share the PM-A-08 docs commit.
verdicts.remediation: Move the green-gate paragraph (:62-65) up to sit after the pointer list (:28-35), ahead of the LibKa0s paragraph and the provenance line. Keep the perf-decline paragraph after them. Content stays unchanged.

verdicts.assessment: The `/pm profile <name>` placeholders at README.md:65 and :229 are real and player-visible, because CurseForge strips <name>. This is a recurrence (9bceeab). The 1.2.0 row's unprefixed tail is the same contributor-facing 'Released on lint, tests and complexity only…' line as LH-A-07, not a player highlight.
verdicts.remediation: Write the argument bare at :65 and :229 (for example `/pm profile Raid`). Delete the 'Released on lint, tests and complexity only…' line from the 1.2.0 row instead of prefixing it, to match LH-A-07. Run the de-AI pass. Optional upstream follow-up: a dev-copilot sync-docs/bump-version check that flags <...> placeholders in README.md.

verdicts.assessment: launcher.md:78 makes the release-note sentence a MUST at each addon's next release, which for MultiMeters was 1.1.0. The 1.1.0 row (README.md:97) omits it. The finding names the wrong old path, though. At 1.0.1-release the row was profile-root `minimap.hide` with invert = true (settings/Schema.lua:1168), not global.minimap.hide. It went through Schema_Paths' toDisplay/toStored seam, so the CLI value was probably already in display ('shown') terms. If so, the standard's generic '<not v>' mapping would be wrong for MM.
verdicts.remediation: Check how 1.0.1 handled `/mm set minimap.hide <v>`: whether the CLI went through the toStored/toDisplay inversion seam in settings/Schema_Paths.lua. Then append one concrete sentence without placeholders to the 1.1.0 row (or the next release row), for example 'since 1.1.0, `/mm set minimap.hide true` is `/mm set global.minimap.shown true`', or 'false' if the CLI used stored terms. Run the de-AI pass and do not bump the version.
